title: The rooftop garden
summary: The neighbours in a grey apartment building turn their flat roof into something nobody expected.
paragraphs: For years the roof of number 14 Calle Lirio was just a flat grey space with an old water tank and a few broken chairs. Nobody went up there except the man who checked the {{aerial}}. Then, one spring, Amal from the third floor carried up a bag of earth and three tomato plants.

At first the other neighbours were {{doubtful}}. "It's too windy," said Mr Gil from the first floor. "The birds will eat everything," said the young couple on the fourth. But Amal watered her plants every evening, and by June there were small green tomatoes. Mr Gil came up to look. The next week he brought a pot of basil.

By the end of the summer, half the building had a pot or a box on the roof. There were peppers, strawberries, mint and one very {{ambitious}} lemon tree. The young couple built a wooden bench from old {{pallets}}. Someone put up lights. On warm evenings people sat there after dinner, talking and watching the sunset over the city.

The garden changed more than the roof. Neighbours who had only said "good morning" in the lift for ten years now knew each other's names, jobs and problems. When Mrs Ortega was in hospital, other people watered her herbs and fed her cat. When the children on the second floor had a birthday, the party was on the roof.

Now there is a list on the door to the stairs. It shows who waters the plants each day and when the next "harvest dinner" will be. The water tank is still there, painted with flowers by the children. And every spring, Amal goes up first with a bag of earth, because a garden, she says, has to be {{started}} again every year.

aerial.meaning: a piece of metal on a roof that receives television signals

doubtful.meaning: not sure that something is true or will happen

ambitious.meaning: wanting to do something difficult or big

pallets.meaning: flat wooden structures used to carry goods

questions.question: Who started the garden?
options: Mr Gil from the first floor
The young couple on the fourth floor
The children on the second floor
questions.explanation: Amal carried up a bag of earth and three tomato plants.

questions.question: What were the neighbours worried about at first?
questions.explanation: Mr Gil said it was too windy and the couple said the birds would eat everything.

questions.question: How did the garden change the neighbours?
options: They argued more about the roof.
They got to know each other and helped each other.
questions.explanation: Neighbours now knew each other's names and problems, and they helped Mrs Ortega.

questions.question: What does Amal say about a garden?
options: It has to be started again every year.
It should be on the ground, not the roof.
questions.explanation: She says a garden has to be started again every year.
